citation: West, M. R., Morton, B. A., & Herlihy, C. M. (2016). Achievement Network's Investing in Innovation Expansion: Impacts on Educator Practice and Student Achievement (Research Paper, March 2016). Cambridge, MA: Center for Education Policy Research, Harvard University. Supported by U.S. Department of Education i3 grant U396C100771. ERIC ED565458.
report_number: CEPR Harvard Research Paper, March 2016 (i3 grant U396C100771); ERIC ED565458; WWC Study 84085
design: Matched-pair school-randomized RCT (cluster RCT, assignment = school). Two recruitment waves; Year 2 (end-of-treatment) full intent-to-treat student impact sample = 89 schools (45 treatment, 44 control) across 5 districts in 4 'networks' (Eastern Massachusetts [Boston/Chelsea], Springfield MA, Chicago IL, Jefferson Parish LA); ~21,000 students in Grades 3-8 (62% elementary G3-5, 38% middle G6-8); 87% FRPL-eligible. Intervention = Achievement Network (ANet) data-driven instruction PD: interim assessments + online data platform/reporting + coaching/support for using data; control = business-as-usual (schools used their own interim assessments and district data support; no restriction on control activity). Subjects measured = ELA (reading) and Math on summative state tests.
problems: Effect sizes are taken directly from the report's exec-summary Table ES.2 and detailed Tables 5.1 (math) and 5.2 (reading). The reported 'impact estimate' is already a standardized impact (the Year-2 state test outcome was standardized within state, subject, and grade using state means/SDs, so the impact coefficient is in pooled state-SD units = a standardized mean difference d). It comes from cluster-adjusted OLS with school-pair dummy variables plus baseline achievement, demographics, and grade fixed effects -> pretest-adjusted and cluster-adjusted (set cluster_adjusted=true; reported SE is the cluster-adjusted SE of d). Hedges g = J*d with J~1.0000 given N>21,000 (g equals the reported impact). No design-effect ICC is reported anywhere in the paper, so icc is left null (spec: never guess an ICC). No raw posttest means/SDs by arm are reported (outcomes were pre-standardized), so mean/sd fields are null. The report standardizes by the STATE distribution SD (within subject x grade), not by the analytic-sample pooled SD; g_method notes this. The contrast is TPD vs business-as-usual, but the exec summary notes control schools were not barred from administering their own interim assessments / receiving district data support, so the estimate is ANet's impact OVER AND ABOVE typical district-led data efforts (a conservative/active-ish control). The TPD-goal registry coding 'TPD for digital tools' is interpretable as ANet's online interim-assessment data platform/reporting tools; the substantive intervention is data-driven-instruction PD. The two FULL-sample rows (math, reading; N=89 schools) are the report's main confirmatory ITT contrasts. The two REDUCED-sample rows (69 schools = only treatment schools that continued with ANet for both years plus their matched pairs) are a non-randomised post-hoc subset, so they are flagged outcome_role=subgroup / is_full_sample=false and are provided for completeness only (the full-sample rows should be preferred for the meta-analysis). Grade-level, network, FRPL, and prior-performance subgroup rows from Tables 5.1/5.2 were not extracted as separate effect sizes (they are non-randomised subgroups of the same outcomes already captured by the overall rows). Teacher/leader survey outcomes (Tables 4.4, Figures 4.2.a-c) were skipped per spec (not student achievement).
